meta.title: Analyst assumptions - kept strictly separate from the verified fact ledger
meta.warning: Nothing in this file is a verified fact. Every number here is a judgement, is used only by the projection model, and is labelled as an assumption everywhere it appears on the site. Changing any of these changes the ranking of the strategies - which is why the site publishes the sensitivity grid rather than a single answer.

assumptions.label: Base capitalisation rate for a single-tenant QSR with about ten years of remaining term, Central Los Angeles
assumptions.basis: No government body publishes transaction cap rates (flagged U-14). Anchored to the verified 10-year Treasury of 4.86% plus a 0.39% risk premium, which is where long-term net-lease single-tenant QSR trades have generally cleared. It is an assumption, not evidence.

assumptions.label: Cap rate widening per year of remaining lease term below ten years
assumptions.value: +10 bp per year, capped at 125 bp
assumptions.basis: Buyers price exit risk. Ten years is the conventional threshold below which lenders and buyers begin to discount; the floor of the resulting cap rate is set at 4.50%.

assumptions.label: Share of a move in the 10-year Treasury that passes into the cap rate
assumptions.basis: Net-lease cap rates are rate-sensitive but not mechanically linked; empirical pass-through is partial.

assumptions.label: Annual NOI growth, base case
assumptions.basis: Bracketed by the verified local CPI-U of +3.7% (F53) and the statutory 3.5% ceiling on state minimum-wage indexation (S15). 2.0% represents a fixed-bump lease, 3.7% a full-CPI lease.

assumptions.label: Remaining lease term at valuation date
assumptions.basis: Midpoint of the Owner's stated 2030-2035 expiry window. The true value is not known (flagged U-03) and is the single most important unknown in the analysis.

assumptions.label: Probability the tenant renews at expiry if the Owner takes no action
assumptions.basis: Assumption. Supports the base case only; the model reports results at 40% and 90% as well.

assumptions.label: Downtime and releasing cost if the tenant does not renew
assumptions.value: 18 months at 50% of prior NOI, plus 6% of value in leasing costs
assumptions.basis: A dark drive-through is hard to re-let; fast-food boxes are purpose-built. Assumption.

assumptions.label: Terms the Owner could realistically obtain in a 2027 extension
assumptions.value: +10 years at in-place rent, 3.0% annual escalators
assumptions.basis: Assumption used to size the extension strategy; the actual offer is unknown. Tenant's own 10-K disclosure is that it 'generally' renews at then-current market rates, but that statement was not re-verified this session (flagged U-16).

assumptions.label: Cost of sale
assumptions.value: 2.50% brokerage, plus 1.10 per 1,000 county transfer tax, plus 0.45% city base tax, plus 4.0% Measure ULA where the price reaches $5,400,000
assumptions.basis: Transfer taxes are verified (F86-F89). Brokerage is an assumption.

assumptions.label: Blended tax on a taxable sale
assumptions.basis: Built from the verified CA top rate of 12.30% (F91) and federal components: 25% on the unrecaptured Section 1250 slice (30% of the gain) and 23.8% (20% capital gain plus 3.8% net investment income tax) on the rest. Federal rates are standard statutory rates and are NOT separately verified in this session.

assumptions.label: Taxable gain as a share of gross sale price
assumptions.basis: Basis and depreciation history are unknown (flagged U-06). This is the assumption that moves the after-tax comparison most after the cap rate.

assumptions.label: Unlevered total return on reinvested proceeds after a taxable sale
assumptions.basis: Cash yield 5.50% with no growth, i.e. a diversified net-lease position bought at today's rates. Assumption.

assumptions.label: Unlevered total return on a Section 1031 replacement portfolio
assumptions.basis: Cash yield 6.25%, growth deferred. The 0.75% uplift over A12 reflects the larger investable base and access to non-urban markets, not a claim about any specific asset. Assumption.

assumptions.label: Blended tax on annual operating income
assumptions.basis: Federal top rate plus the verified CA top rate. Assumes a high-bracket individual Owner, which is the conservative case for a hold decision.

assumptions.label: Annual probability of a hazard event that impairs value by more than 20%
assumptions.basis: Analyst judgement informed by the January 2025 Los Angeles fire pair and regional seismic exposure. The parcel-level hazard class is unknown (flagged U-07, U-08), so this is deliberately coarse.

assumptions.label: Annual probability of a total loss
assumptions.basis: Analyst judgement. Insurance recovery is assumed to be partial and slow, which is why a total loss is not modelled as a full recovery.

assumptions.label: Horizon
assumptions.basis: Long enough to cover the full expiry window plus a post-expiry cycle, without pretending to forecast beyond a generation.

assumptions.label: Monte Carlo trials and seed
assumptions.basis: Deterministic and reproducible: the same seed always produces the same file.

assumptions.label: In-place rent versus market rent
assumptions.basis: Unknown (flagged U-02). If the in-place rent is below market, the extension strategy worsens and the sale strategy improves, because a buyer would reprice to market at expiry.

assumptions.label: Share of the reinvestment total return taken as taxable current income rather than appreciation
assumptions.basis: A net-lease portfolio bought at today's yields distributes most of its return as rent, with the remainder as slow appreciation. Assumption.
